dimension: # PRELIMINARY / ILLUSTRATIVE / NOT FOR EXTERNAL CLAIMS
option: banner row, not a design option
what_it_changes_in_the_model: nothing in this file is a finding, a recommendation or evidence; every numeric value is tier 5 (illustrative)
already_implemented_by: not applicable
notes: Prepared 2026-09-02, banner row added 2026-09-03. Cells marked (pre-R004 run) are model outputs from the Phase A ablation abl_20260902_phaseA. Protocol revisions R004 and R005 (2026-09-03) changed the capacity ramp, the cost ledger, the opening-stock cohorts and the reserved-line convention, and R007 (2026-09-03) changed the supplier-capacity gate, the deterministic screen's treatment of reserved capacity and the accrual of reservation fees; every run made before 2026-09-03 is therefore superseded for quantitative use and must be re-run before any figure here is quoted. Companion document: architecture_taxonomy.md.

option: aqueous small-molecule terminally sterilizable vial (e.g. sodium bicarbonate 8.4%)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: product dossier sets batch size, shelf life, status_quo_utilization and the release-component vector; permits a parametric-release scenario instead of the 14 d sterility hold
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: sterility-related delay; release queue; capacity shortfall (through status_quo_utilization)
already_implemented_by: every LVP and SVP holder that autoclaves; Baxter North Cove
notes: route is not published per marketed presentation, so the archetype cannot yet be assigned from public data (prior-art review section 7 item 11)

option: aqueous small-molecule aseptically filled vial (e.g. norepinephrine)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: keeps the 14 d sterility component as the argmax of the release set; no parametric route available
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none (release is not binding); it is the archetype the binding capacity and inventory modes were measured on
already_implemented_by: Pfizer/Hospira; Baxter; Hikma
notes: beachhead verification failed for norepinephrine on 2026-07-16 and the EDA End-to-End project already names it (F13-S24)

option: ready-to-administer premix bag or prefilled syringe
what_it_changes_in_the_model: shorter effective shelf life and a different container-closure; changes site_fg_days economics and the BUD schedule
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: inventory timing; contract insufficiency (a differentiated product can carry a price)
already_implemented_by: SCA Pharmaceuticals; Fagron; QuVa; Baxter RTU premix
notes: if made under 503B the at-risk BUD table caps dating at 6/14/28 days (F11-S45)

option: lyophilized small-molecule vial
what_it_changes_in_the_model: longer production_cycle_days and a second unit operation; removes terminal sterilization from the option set
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none directly; it raises capacity cost per unit
already_implemented_by: Fresenius Melrose Park; Hikma; Gland
notes: WHO QAS/16.682 scores sterile forms as unfavourable for start-up manufacture (F12-S32)

option: concentrate for dilution as the pooled presentation
what_it_changes_in_the_model: one upstream SKU serving several downstream presentations; would need a multi-SKU demand model the engine does not have
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: demand variance; demand covariance (pooling); inventory timing
already_implemented_by: the historical default, pushed against for 25 years
notes: Joint Commission and FDA label rules restrict concentrates at the bedside; this is a safety objection, not a modelling one

option: cytotoxic or high-potency injectable
what_it_changes_in_the_model: forces dedicated facilities or HBEL-justified segregation; blocks the shared-portfolio node
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it raises fixed quality cost and replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: dedicated oncology sterile plants across the industry
notes: 21 CFR 211.42(d) and the beta-lactam guidance make this incompatible with dimension 'product portfolio' options above one family

option: biologic or vaccine drug product
what_it_changes_in_the_model: out of archetype for both frozen product dossiers; would require a new dossier set and a cold-chain lane model
already_implemented_by: Pfizer/BioNTech; Moderna with Lonza and Catalent
notes: the hub-and-spoke precedent is real but was never at microplant scale

option: large-volume parenteral or diluent (sterile water, saline)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: very high volume, very low unit price; makes annualized capital per unit the dominant cost term
already_implemented_by: Baxter; B. Braun; DEKA Caspian demonstration units
notes: the 2024 Helene episode is the documented shortage case; price per unit is lower than the $1.47 vial the readiness question already fails on

option: hospital pharmacy direct (single health system)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: ContractTerms purchaser and beneficiary are the same party; committed volume is small relative to a node's capacity
already_implemented_by: QuVa (over 3,000 US hospitals); Leiters; SCA
notes: CMS pays eligible hospitals for a six-month buffer, which funds the buyer's stock and not the maker's readiness (LSD-S3)

option: group purchasing organization (Vizient, Premier, HealthTrust)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: one purchaser aggregating demand; makes committed_units_per_year large enough to matter but concentrates default risk
already_implemented_by: Vizient NES and Reserve; Premier ProvideGx; HealthTrust SIMS
notes: three GPOs cover over 90% of US hospitals, so selling outside the channel means selling against it

option: hospital consortium that co-owns the asset
what_it_changes_in_the_model: capital requirement is shared; utilization is contracted by construction; payer and beneficiary coincide
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: contract insufficiency; low utilization; capacity shortfall
already_implemented_by: STAQ Pharma (health-system-owned 503B); Civica; Premier equity in Exela
notes: the documented instances are 503B or an ANDA co-investment, not a co-owned distributed network

option: federal purchaser (BARDA, ASPR, SNS, DLA)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: activation condition and allocation rights are exercisable by the buyer; capital may be granted rather than raised
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: contract insufficiency; capacity shortfall; insufficient surge headroom
already_implemented_by: Project BioShield; CIADM; DLA Warstopper; Phlow
notes: advance purchase is implemented for countermeasures only (F10-S29); BioMaP entry needs MRL 6 with cost share

option: state or regional programme (CalRx-type)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a purchaser with a statutory mandate but no manufacturing licence; Telo would hold the application
already_implemented_by: CalRx (naloxone white-label, contracted insulin); Virginia EDA coalition
notes: no state has licensed and operated a generic sterile-injectable plant

option: ANDA holder or incumbent manufacturer (Telo sells capacity to them)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: Telo is a listed contract site; the customer owns the application, so gates G01 and G02 sit with them
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: commissioning delay; capacity shortfall; contract insufficiency
already_implemented_by: every merchant sterile CDMO (Simtra, Curia, Jubilant, GRAM)
notes: the standard contract shape puts committed capacity obligations on the maker without minimum purchase on the buyer (LCDM-S14)

option: CDMO or 503B operator buying a service (lab, software, qualification)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no drug revenue; the model would need a fee channel it does not have
already_implemented_by: Korber, Veeva, MasterControl, Leucine sell here today
notes: the two largest 503B operators already run rapid sterility on site, which bounds a hub-lab offer (F4-S11, F4-S14)

option: wholesaler or distributor (McKesson, Cencora, Cardinal)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need an allocation-layer model the engine does not have
prior_art_source_ids: no external precedent found (search: landscape/shortage_data_supply_risk.md section 6.10)
already_implemented_by: none found
notes: the landscape sweep did not cover wholesaler allocation systems, which probably hold the real-time availability data

option: unit sale of finished drug product under Telo's own application
what_it_changes_in_the_model: break_even_price is the whole annual cost divided by delivered units; Telo carries every gate
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none directly; it is the only mechanism the cost model currently prices
already_implemented_by: Civica (own ANDAs plus partner supply)
notes: the model never infers a price from a cost (protocol 5.2); a price needs HA-11 or HA-24 evidence

option: unit sale under a partner's application (own-label distributor)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: removes the application-holder gate from Telo and with it the commissioning path, but also the data rights
already_implemented_by: Civica label-and-NDC over Xellia's ANDA; own-label distributors are an FDA category
notes: no manufacturing asset is involved, so no service mechanism in the engine changes

option: contract manufacturing fee (Telo as the CDMO)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: revenue per batch rather than per unit; utilization becomes the customer's problem, not Telo's
already_implemented_by: Simtra, GRAM, Jubilant, Curia
notes: the engine has no revenue side at all, so this is an accounting change outside the simulation

option: reservation fee plus execution fee (capacity option)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: reserved sites carry only the reservation fee when not owned (R004); take_or_pay_fraction charges committed volume whether or not the line runs
already_implemented_by: EU FAB (about EUR 160M for twelve months); BARDA CIADM; commercial Lonza and WuXi clauses
notes: no disclosed pharmaceutical contract states both fees; every SEC reservation fee is redacted (F3-S53, F3-S55)

option: availability payment untied to units shipped
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need a payer entity and a readiness price the model does not contain
already_implemented_by: FHWA P3 concessions; NHS England delinked antimicrobial subscription
notes: four counsel questions gate this (anti-kickback, antitrust after the 2023 safety-zone withdrawal, 340B and Medicaid rebate mechanics, FAR Part 16)

option: software subscription per site or per batch
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no service mechanism changes; only deviation_rate_factor and investigation_duration_factor are available, and they touch the quality workflow only
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none binding; deviation and investigation duration only
already_implemented_by: Korber PAS-X (over half the top 30), Veeva, MasterControl, Tulip, Leucine
notes: the protocol forbids an OS effect on release time or capacity, so software cannot reach any binding mechanism in this engine

option: laboratory testing service fee (hub laboratory)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: moves QC cost off the site ledger; does not change release latency unless the method changes
already_implemented_by: Creative Testing Solutions (five donor-testing labs); contract labs recognised by 21 CFR 207.1
notes: value is bounded because the large 503B operators already run rapid sterility on site (prior-art review 6.5)

option: grant or cost-plus government funding
what_it_changes_in_the_model: capital arrives without a contribution margin; the break-even calculation stops meaning anything
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it relieves capital, not service
already_implemented_by: Phlow (cost-plus-fixed-fee); APIIC and Antheia readiness grants; Virginia to Civica
notes: not a durable revenue mechanism; Phlow was still not profitable as of May 2026, six years into a 2020-2030 contract, though its spokesman says it is on track (LNPM-S09, LNPM-S11)

option: single large conventional plant
what_it_changes_in_the_model: one site, one common-cause geography group; capacity above scale 1.05 waits capacity_expansion_days (365 d)
already_implemented_by: Civica Petersburg; Nexus; Jubilant Spokane
notes: greenfield timelines observed in the landscape run to years, not months (landscape section 5)

option: small gloveless isolator workcell
what_it_changes_in_the_model: small batch_size_units at a high batches_per_year; node capacity is quadratic in capacity_factor unless the generic builder is used (MD-8)
already_implemented_by: Cytiva SA25/Microcell (65+ sold); Syntegon Versynta; SKAN VarioSys; Steriline
notes: hardware novelty cannot be claimed; purchase-to-GMP is 6 to 15 months for the workcell alone (LAMD-S16)

option: prefabricated cleanroom POD inside a shell building
what_it_changes_in_the_model: shortens commissioning_days relative to a greenfield build but not the regulatory tail
already_implemented_by: G-CON with Pfizer PCMM, Just-Evotec, NIIMBL Project Blackhawk
notes: no POD is documented hosting an inspected sterile fill-finish line for an approved injectable

option: trailer or container mobile cleanroom
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need a mobility clock, requalification after movement and a registration state per unit; none exists in the engine
already_implemented_by: Germfree (100+ mobile cleanrooms since 2015); Odulair; KeyPlants for Ferring; BioNTainer
notes: family 14's verdict is that the qualification and release clock restarts after a move, so mobility is slower than shipped inventory

option: hospital-hosted point-of-care unit
what_it_changes_in_the_model: serves one region only; would need a per-hospital demand model rather than four regions
already_implemented_by: On Demand Pharmaceuticals with Germfree at North Mississippi Health Services (503A pilot)
notes: the pilot ran under 503A, not under an approved application; roughly 12,000 syringes in six months

option: leased or reserved suite inside an already registered plant
what_it_changes_in_the_model: exists_at_t0 true with commissioning_days near zero; buys registered capacity instead of building it
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: commissioning delay; capacity shortfall; insufficient surge headroom
already_implemented_by: every CDMO reservation; BARDA FFMN and the 2021 CDMO network
notes: the decomposition puts this at exactly 0.000000 commissioning delta against a 730 d build (pre-R004 run)

option: no facility at all (contracts and coordination only)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no site rows; every service mechanism runs through partners' capacity and through inventory
already_implemented_by: Civica 2018-2023, which then reversed and built Petersburg
notes: GAO records contamination control as a stated reason for the reversal; the asset-light form is documented to be unstable

option: micro (batch under about 0.1x the central batch)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: node_scale about 0.1; fixed quality cost per unit rises roughly as the inverse of scale
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it worsens fixed quality cost and low utilization
already_implemented_by: Syntegon Versynta microBatch (120 to 500 containers/hour)
notes: media-fill and cleaning-validation economics set a minimum campaign size nobody has published (F6-S11, F6-S04)

option: small (node_scale about 0.2 to 0.4, the frozen default)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the value the frozen S5 and S6 designs use; four nodes at 0.35 do not cover the sodium bicarbonate deficit
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: capacity shortfall (partially); inventory timing (stock is closer to demand)
already_implemented_by: Cytiva SA25 class installations
notes: distributed nodes are the worst-performing build architecture in the run for sodium bicarbonate (pre-R004 run)

option: mid (node_scale about 0.5 to 1.0)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: raises capital and fixed cost per node while cutting the number of nodes needed for the same capacity
already_implemented_by: Gland (28 lines); GRAM
notes: no source gives minimum economic scale for generic sterile fill-finish (prior-art review, family 12 row)

option: equal to the central plant
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a second full plant; doubles the fixed quality and validation blocks unless they are shared
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: capacity shortfall; common-cause failures (if genuinely independent)
already_implemented_by: Fresenius Melrose Park (250 products, 160M vials/yr); Hikma
notes: 24.1% to 33.0% of annual cost is fixed quality and 4.7% to 18.0% is replicated validation, both per site (pre-R004 run)

option: expansion of the incumbent line above the status-quo scale of 1.05
what_it_changes_in_the_model: capacity_factor above 1.05 is an expansion and waits capacity_expansion_days (365 d, tier 5) since R004
already_implemented_by: Hikma ($1B by 2030); Baxter (over $2.5B in a decade); Fresenius (over USD 250M)
notes: instant_expansion restores the pre-R004 free instant capacity and is for a labelled sensitivity only

option: single central site serving all regions
what_it_changes_in_the_model: one site row; delivery_days to every region; no cc_os or cc_quality node group
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it is the reference topology
already_implemented_by: the status quo for almost every US generic injectable
notes: sodium bicarbonate S0 is capacity-short by construction at status_quo_utilization 1.245

option: central plus N regional nodes, each serving its own region
what_it_changes_in_the_model: serves=own_region; a stockout in one region cannot be covered by another except through emergency_transfers
already_implemented_by: PET producers under 21 CFR 212; multi-site 503B operators; UK modular manufacture
notes: the frozen S5 and S6 shape; every node shares cc_api, cc_vial, cc_os and cc_quality

option: central plus N regional nodes serving all regions (pooled)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: serves=all; pools node capacity against regional demand shocks at the cost of longer lanes
already_implemented_by: any multi-site manufacturer shipping nationally; QuVa forward distribution centres
notes: pooling is available in the engine through the serves field and is not exercised by any frozen strategy

option: hub producing bulk solution, spokes filling
what_it_changes_in_the_model: an extra_supplier with its own lead time feeding the fill sites; the hub becomes a new single point of failure
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost; commissioning delay (spokes are simpler)
prior_art_source_ids: F4-S2, F4-S3, F4-S4, Lreg-S8, Lreg-S13, F5-S16
already_implemented_by: Pfizer/BioNTech (Andover to Kalamazoo and Puurs); Moderna with Lonza and Catalent
notes: no approved US example located for an aqueous small-molecule injectable; EMA expects refiltration if bulk is not filled within 24 hours

option: central quality laboratory serving distributed production
what_it_changes_in_the_model: moves QC cost off each site; release latency unchanged unless the method changes
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: Pfizer central labs at Chesterfield and Andover; Creative Testing Solutions
notes: 21 CFR 207.1 recognises control and contract laboratories; no FDA requirement that sterility testing occur on the fill site was found

option: virtual network of third-party registered sites
what_it_changes_in_the_model: cdmo_reserved site plans with activation_lead_days and activation_failure_probability; no Telo capital
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: commissioning delay; capacity shortfall; contract insufficiency
already_implemented_by: BARDA FFMN 2013 and the 2021 CDMO network; EU FAB; CEPI VMFN
notes: independence is not free: partners sharing an API source stay in the same common-cause group

option: two sites inside one region (intra-region redundancy)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: since R005 nodes may exceed the region count and are placed round-robin; a second node in a region joins that region's geography group
already_implemented_by: large operators with two lines on one campus
notes: redundancy inside one region buys less than redundancy across regions, by construction

option: coordination layer across independently owned sites, no Telo site
what_it_changes_in_the_model: not representable: the engine has one owner and no cross-owner entity
already_implemented_by: none found; HDA reports the federal control tower has no two-way communication
notes: a contracting and antitrust problem before it is a software problem (Sherman Act, DOJ/FTC monitoring)

option: API synthesis
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need an internal API supplier with its own capacity and disruption draw; today API is an external Supplier with a lead time
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: supplier concentration; common-cause failures on the API group
already_implemented_by: Phlow; API Innovation Center; Bright Path Laboratories
notes: API onshoring is orthogonal to both dominant documented shortage causes (prior-art review, does-not-survive list)

option: bulk solution compounding and sterile filtration
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the hub half of a hub-and-spoke; representable only as an extra_supplier with a lead time, with no hold-time expiry
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: no implemented US example located for an aqueous small-molecule injectable
notes: a multi-day bulk hold is the unresolved regulatory question (prior-art review section 7 item 3)

option: aseptic fill-finish
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the site archetype the whole engine is built around
already_implemented_by: Pfizer/Hospira, Fresenius, Hikma, Simtra, GRAM
notes: capex observed in the landscape ranges from $100M to over $1B per expansion

option: terminal sterilization only, as a contract step
what_it_changes_in_the_model: adds a transport leg and a queue after filling; would need a post-fill stage the engine does not model
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: sterility-related delay (through the route, not through the step)
already_implemented_by: contract terminal sterilizers
notes: only meaningful for a product whose route is terminal, which is dimension 'sterilization/release route'

option: labeling, packaging and final configuration
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a postponement step with no sterile exposure; not representable without a multi-SKU model
already_implemented_by: PCI packaging centres; Sharp; Civica label-and-NDC; 503B repackaging
notes: 21 CFR 211.130(b) has permitted late labeling since 1978; the constraint is identification control, not the concept

option: QC testing and release only
what_it_changes_in_the_model: changes where cost sits, not when product is released, unless the method changes
already_implemented_by: Creative Testing Solutions; ScanRDI at QuVa; SCA rapid sterility
notes: the hub-lab intervention point is real but bounded (prior-art review 6.5)

option: no manufacturing step (coordination or software only)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the engine offers deviation_rate_factor and investigation_duration_factor and nothing else
already_implemented_by: Vizient, Premier ProvideGx, Bluesight, USP Medicine Supply Map
notes: the money in shortage response already flows to these vendors

option: inventory holding and distribution only
what_it_changes_in_the_model: region_base_stock, region_reorder_point_days and safety_stock_days with no site of Telo's own
already_implemented_by: DLA Warstopper VMI; SNS VMI; QuVa forward DCs; Vizient NES
notes: the frozen regional review rule is the single largest service lever in the whole ablation (MD-3)

option: Telo holds the application and a resident quality unit at every site
what_it_changes_in_the_model: fixed quality cost and validation cost replicate per site; gate G13 applies per unit
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it is the cost-maximal option
already_implemented_by: conventional multi-site manufacturers
notes: 24.1% to 33.0% of annual cost sits in this block and no service mechanism touches it (pre-R004 run)

option: Telo holds the application; one quality unit spans every unit (DME-style)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would let fixed_cost_factor fall below 1 legitimately; the engine has no shared-quality-unit object, only a per-site multiplier
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: nobody for approved sterile injectables; the DME rule is proposed only
notes: the proposal requires one management, a unified quality system and a single legal entity registrant, and excludes contract units

option: a partner holds the application; Telo is a listed contract site
what_it_changes_in_the_model: gates G01 and G02 move to the partner; Telo's commissioning is a supplement, not an application
already_implemented_by: every merchant CDMO relationship
notes: data rights and channel conflict are the price; neither is in the model

option: Telo is an own-label distributor of a partner's product
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no manufacturing entity at all; only inventory and contracts remain
already_implemented_by: Civica over Xellia's ANDA
notes: this is a distribution business with a manufacturing story attached; say so if proposed

option: 503B outsourcing facility registration, no approved application
what_it_changes_in_the_model: pathway 503b; the validator refuses durable=true; eligibility is a time-varying state driven by the shortage listing
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: regulatory unavailability (it creates it); capacity shortfall (short term)
already_implemented_by: 97 registered facilities on FDA's table 8/28/2026
notes: no injectable is on the 503B bulks list and FDA does not treat backorders as clinical need; never a durable core

option: no regulatory status (software or data vendor)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no gate applies to Telo, but records the product generates are GMP records for the customer
already_implemented_by: Veeva, Korber, MasterControl, Tulip, Leucine
notes: Warning Letter 320-26-58 is the first documented enforcement applying 21 CFR 211.22(c) to AI-generated GMP records

option: a government body or nonprofit holds the licence
what_it_changes_in_the_model: capital and default risk move to the public balance sheet; Telo becomes an operator
already_implemented_by: California CDPH is the named manufacturer on BabyBIG STN 125034; seven US nonprofit drug companies
notes: one orphan biologic does not generalise to a multi-product generic portfolio; five nonprofits told GAO their exempt status is threatened

option: none
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no OS entity; sites do not share cc_os
already_implemented_by: the status quo
notes: worth stating: a shared OS version is itself a common-cause group in this model, so the OS has a negative service term

option: electronic batch record and MES documentation wedge
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no representable effect; the protocol forbids an OS effect on release time or capacity
already_implemented_by: Korber PAS-X, Siemens, Emerson, Rockwell, MasterControl, Tulip, Apprentice, Leucine
notes: a crowded market with a stated incumbent weakness (Rockwell concedes MES is expensive and slow to implement)

option: deviation and CAPA orchestration
what_it_changes_in_the_model: deviation_rate_factor and investigation_duration_factor, which touch the quality workflow only, never release time or capacity
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: deviation and rejection (non-binding in Phase A)
already_implemented_by: Veeva (300+ customers), Sparta TrackWise, MasterControl, ValGenesis
notes: the deviation mode is statistically resolved in 9 of 16 cells and flips none of them

option: campaign scheduling inside one owner
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need multi-product campaigns and changeover, which the engine does not have
already_implemented_by: Werum/sedApta, Leucine (one instance across 30 Cipla sites), Apprentice
notes: MILP and RTN scheduling formulations are published; a fill-finish scheduler with media-fill and cleaning-validation constraints is not

option: capacity coordination across independent owners
what_it_changes_in_the_model: not representable; the engine has one owner
already_implemented_by: none live; Axio Lattice in development, L7 EXCHANGE estimated 2027
notes: the barrier is antitrust and the absence of a payer, not software

option: drift detection and mandatory-hold decision support
what_it_changes_in_the_model: release stays conventional; the model would need a hold-decision channel that does not shorten release
already_implemented_by: Sartorius SIMCA-online, Aizon, Basetwo, Quartic sell the monitoring half today
notes: the open part is a validated abstention mechanism and per-site validity, which are instruments rather than products

option: internal control system for Telo's own network, not sold
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no revenue; keeps cc_os as a shared group across Telo sites
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none binding; it adds a common-cause group
already_implemented_by: Leucine at Cipla; Apprentice CMN; Pfizer's internal programme
notes: this is the honest form of the OS in a manufacturing architecture: an internal cost, not a product

option: none; conventional compendial release (R0)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the frozen release component vector; sterility 14 d is the argmax, plus about 2 d serial QA
already_implemented_by: every approved sterile injectable released on USP <71>
notes: the frozen release-constraints memo misquotes the 2004 guidance on this point and should be corrected (prior-art review 5.1)

option: validated analytical release of chemical attributes (R1/R2)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: removes at most 2 of 16 release days; worth at most +0.002114 fill anywhere in the run (pre-R004 run)
already_implemented_by: RTRT is mature for oral solid dose; no sterile injectable precedent
notes: S6 is numerically identical to S5 on every service metric and costs 2.7M to 3.1M USD/yr more (pre-R004 run)

option: validated rapid microbiological method for the sterility test
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would cut the sterility component from 14 d toward about 5 d; a labelled validated-rapid-micro scenario, never a silent reduction
already_implemented_by: Novartis (FDA, EMA, MHRA acceptances 2008-2010); ScanRDI at QuVa; SCA
notes: Novartis quantified a residual environmental-monitoring wait after moving sterility to 5 days, so the pole may just move

option: parametric release on a terminally sterilized product
what_it_changes_in_the_model: removes the sterility hold rather than compressing it; the only mechanism in the sweep that does
already_implemented_by: FDA-approved applicants since 1985 under CPG 490.200
notes: FDA's QbR FAQ ties the abbreviated route to the identical facility, autoclave, container-closure, parameters and load patterns, so it may be a per-site asset

option: release before the sterility result under a notification protocol
what_it_changes_in_the_model: not available for the archetypes in scope; PET, short-lived radiopharmaceuticals and the 503B at-risk table only
already_implemented_by: 21 CFR 212.70(e); 211.165(a); PROVENGE; 503B Appendix B Table D
notes: the 503B version prices the aseptic-versus-terminal choice at 6 versus 14 days of at-risk dating

option: selective prediction with abstention as decision support only
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no release component changes; abstention is never counted as release
already_implemented_by: no vendor found selling one under the FDA AI credibility framework or draft Annex 22
notes: the current gate is not operationally useful at its observed risk-coverage frontier; that finding stands

option: site-conditional model validity offered as cross-site equivalence evidence
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would enter through G14 rather than through release time
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: common-cause failures (weakly, as evidence of equivalence)
already_implemented_by: Telo research only; no external precedent
notes: a reviewer may find that per-site conformal coverage is not comparability evidence; that is the falsifier

option: fully centralized manufacture and release
what_it_changes_in_the_model: one site, one quality unit, one geography group
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost (both minimal)
already_implemented_by: the status quo for US generic sterile injectables
notes: concentrates common-cause exposure in one geography

option: centralized manufacture with regional inventory
what_it_changes_in_the_model: region_base_stock or region_reorder_point_days with a single production site
already_implemented_by: Vizient NES supplier-held onshore stock; QuVa forward DCs; Germany's six-month obligation
notes: the cheapest lever that reaches the target in the run, and the one most contaminated by MD-3

option: centralized bulk with regional finishing
what_it_changes_in_the_model: hub supplier plus fill sites; the bulk hold time is the unmodelled constraint
already_implemented_by: Pfizer/BioNTech; Moderna with Lonza and Catalent
notes: no approved US aqueous small-molecule example located; family 4 calls this its most decision-relevant gap

option: centralized quality and release with distributed manufacture
what_it_changes_in_the_model: one quality unit, several sites; not representable as a shared object, only as a per-site cost multiplier
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: Pfizer central labs; the DME proposal (not final)
notes: PharMEDium is the documented warning about one quality organisation spanning several sterile sites under stress

option: fully distributed with per-site release
what_it_changes_in_the_model: each site releases its own product; every site carries its own quality and validation cost
already_implemented_by: PET producers under 21 CFR 212; multi-site 503B operators
notes: this is the architecture the run scores worst for the capacity-short product

option: distributed manufacture that Telo does not own
what_it_changes_in_the_model: cdmo_reserved plans; Telo holds contracts, packages and coordination
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: commissioning delay; capacity shortfall; contract insufficiency
already_implemented_by: BARDA FFMN; EU FAB; CEPI VMFN; Civica 2018-2023
notes: activation latency and qualification burden replace commissioning; neither is free

option: spot sale or GPO award with no commitment
what_it_changes_in_the_model: ContractTerms.mechanism=spot; committed_units_per_year is zero, so no fixed cost is covered
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it is the mechanism that fails the contractability test
already_implemented_by: the default in US generic injectables
notes: the standard shape puts committed capacity obligations on the maker without minimum purchase on the buyer

option: take-or-pay minimum volume
what_it_changes_in_the_model: take_or_pay_fraction charges a share of the reserved line whether or not it runs; sets minimum contracted utilization
already_implemented_by: Civica minimum viable volume contracts (about 50% of expected volume, 3 to 10 years)
notes: the contract text is not public, so whether the MVV is a take-or-pay or a forecast is unverified

option: capacity subscription (periodic fee for reserved capacity)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: reservation fee only when reserved_site_owned=0 (R004); no capital, fixed operations or validation on Telo's ledger
already_implemented_by: DLA Warstopper; NHS England delinked subscription; nothing in US generic sterile capacity
notes: no US purchaser has been found paying a standing reservation fee for sterile shortage-generic capacity

option: capacity option (reservation fee plus execution fee)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the same two-part structure with an explicit strike; activation_threshold_days sets when it is exercised
already_implemented_by: EU FAB; BARDA CIADM ($542.75M Emergent reservation); commercial clauses at Lonza and WuXi
notes: every disclosed reservation fee in the SEC exhibits is redacted, so the price of this instrument is unknown

option: government advance purchase
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a committed buyer at a stated quantity; removes demand risk and with it the utilization problem
already_implemented_by: Project BioShield under 42 U.S.C. 247d-6b(c)(7)
notes: implemented for medical countermeasures only; no federal advance purchase for a routine generic sterile injectable was found

option: availability payment untied to units
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need a readiness price; the engine has no revenue side, so this is arithmetic outside the simulation
already_implemented_by: FHWA P3 concessions; NHS England for patented antimicrobials
notes: no availability-payment contract for a multi-source generic injectable was found anywhere

option: outcome-based reliability agreement
what_it_changes_in_the_model: payment contingent on a measured availability outcome; needs a rating layer and a measurement the model does not produce
already_implemented_by: proposed only: Senate Finance draft Manufacturer Reliability Agreements; HHS MRAP and HRSP concepts
notes: HIRC, ISPE and USP are named as candidate rating layers; none is contractually operative

option: stockpile or vendor-managed rotating inventory
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a third party holds and rotates stock; representable as regional inventory with a different owner
already_implemented_by: DLA Warstopper VMI and Corporate Exigency Contracts; SNS VMI; Premier ProvideGx
notes: who bears the carrying cost is the single most important open question for anyone modelling who pays for resilience

option: site finished-goods buffer only
what_it_changes_in_the_model: site_fg_days; the strongest single relaxation found in the design-space run was site_fg_days 60 to 180
already_implemented_by: standard practice at every manufacturer
notes: site_fg_days is absent from the search space of six of the eight frozen strategies (MD-12)

option: regional safety stock on the frozen reorder-point rule
what_it_changes_in_the_model: reorder_days = lane_days + 1.0 against target_days = safety + lane; decisive in 8 of 16 cells
already_implemented_by: regional distribution centres across the industry
notes: this rule is a model artifact (MD-3) that the protocol never specifies and the optimizer never searched

option: regional base stock with daily review
what_it_changes_in_the_model: region_base_stock=1 reviews daily and orders up to target; the opt-in alternative to the frozen rule
already_implemented_by: standard base-stock practice; Germany and Finland mandate stock levels rather than a review rule
notes: bounds:ss365+base_stock reaches 13 of 16 feasible where bounds:ss365 alone reaches 0; verify before believing

option: upstream API and component reserve
what_it_changes_in_the_model: material_target_days and material_reorder_days; the reorder point now covers at least one batch's draw (R005)
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: component and material availability; supplier concentration
already_implemented_by: Premier ProvideGx (3 to 6 months of API and finished dose); Finland's Act 979/2008; Phlow SAPIR
notes: MD-1 is unfixed: the order-up-to level still scales with the lead time, so a shorter lead cuts the buffer

option: bulk or unlabeled intermediate held as the buffer
what_it_changes_in_the_model: not representable; there is no intermediate inventory stage and no hold-time expiry
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: demand variance; demand covariance; inventory timing
already_implemented_by: BARDA National Pre-Pandemic Influenza Vaccine Stockpile since 2005 (antigen, not aqueous small molecule)
notes: EMA expects refiltration if sterile-filtered bulk is not filled within 24 hours; a validated multi-day hold has no precedent

option: shared national reserve with allocation rights
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need a reserve entity and an allocation rule beyond the four in allocation_policy
already_implemented_by: nobody links a national reserve to several regional manufacturing sites; SAPIR proposes the nearest analogue
notes: the Strategic API Reserve is a line item in one BARDA contract plus bills unenacted across four Congresses

option: rotating hospital inventory funded by the CMS buffer payment
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the stock sits with the buyer; Telo would see a smoother order stream, not a service change
already_implemented_by: CMS pays eligible hospitals for a six-month buffer, explicitly permitting an intermediary to hold it
notes: eligibility is limited to hospitals of 100 beds or fewer outside a chain; reimbursement is not manufacturing cost

option: single API and single vial/stopper supplier
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the status quo; supplier_disruption_days.mean is identical across all eight frozen strategies of each product
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it is the exposure being measured
already_implemented_by: the default for most US generic injectables
notes: supplier concentration is statistically resolved in 11 of 16 cells and flips three

option: second API source qualified and existing at t0
what_it_changes_in_the_model: second_source_exists_at_t0=1 with independent_api_supplier=1; without the second flag the source shares the API group
already_implemented_by: standard dual sourcing; Phlow; API Innovation Center; EU procurement incentives
notes: dual sourcing is the only frozen strategy that clears at fill >= 0.98 in the pre-R004 runs

option: second source qualified on demand
what_it_changes_in_the_model: second_source_qualification_days (365 d, tier 5, range 365 to 1095) before the source is usable
already_implemented_by: the instrument exists (21 CFR 314.70(e), ICH Q12 PACMP); FDA publishes no approved protocols
notes: the FDA carve-out caps the gain at CBE-30, so the asset is worth about 30 days plus predictability

option: standardized ISO container-closure across products
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would reduce component variety and qualification cost; not representable, components are per-product
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: component and material availability; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: ISO 8362-1; SCHOTT adaptiQ and Stevanato EZ-fill nested tubs
notes: every application still qualifies its own container-closure system; a shared package usable by several holders has no precedent

option: an internal hub acting as the bulk supplier
what_it_changes_in_the_model: extra_suppliers with lead_time_days or lead_time_factor and its own common-cause groups
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: Pfizer/BioNTech at biologics scale
notes: the hub has no capacity limit and no hold-time expiry in the engine; both are missing constraints

option: supplier-risk graph subscribed rather than owned
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no model effect; it is an information product
already_implemented_by: USP Medicine Supply Map with the KSM module; Resilinc; Vizient market resiliency score
notes: already implemented and patented in the adjacent shortage-scoring space

option: strategic raw-material reserve held by Telo
what_it_changes_in_the_model: material_target_days raised well above the lead time; MD-1 makes this interact with the lead-time factor in an unintended way
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: component and material availability; supplier concentration
already_implemented_by: Phlow SAPIR CLIN 0004; Finland's substance reserve
notes: the US Strategic API Reserve is proposed, not funded as standing policy

option: one presentation per network
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the engine limit today (MD-15); 94.5% of norepinephrine S5 cost is borne by one presentation at 0.203 utilization (pre-R004 run)
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; it is the source of the low-utilization mode
already_implemented_by: no real sterile plant runs one presentation
notes: the largest unquantified distortion in the cost comparison

option: two to four comparable aqueous presentations
what_it_changes_in_the_model: portfolio_capacity_share and portfolio_fixed_cost_share attribute a share of capacity and fixed cost to this product
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: low utilization; fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: small multi-product sterile sites and CDMO suites
notes: the shares are an accounting proxy; changeover, cleaning validation and campaign sequencing are absent

option: about five or more comparable presentations (the pooling threshold)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the decomposition names roughly five comparable presentations per node as the explicit, testable pooling threshold
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: low utilization; fixed quality cost; replicated validation cost
already_implemented_by: Fresenius Melrose Park (250 products); Hikma (180+ injectables); Gland (28 lines)
notes: no source gives a minimum economic campaign size for generic sterile fill-finish; the threshold is a model output, not evidence

option: broad multi-family portfolio with segregation
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need family constraints, dedicated areas and HBEL carryover limits the engine does not model
already_implemented_by: large generic injectable plants across the industry
notes: 21 CFR 211.42(d) and the beta-lactam guidance make some combinations facility-separating, not scheduling problems

option: shortage-risk-weighted selected portfolio
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a selection layer on top of the portfolio shares; the matching model is not built
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: capacity shortfall (by choosing where it binds); regulatory unavailability
already_implemented_by: Civica selects informally via member pharmacists; USP and Premier score shortage risk
notes: nobody optimises a node's portfolio subject to changeover and family constraints; that is the open combination

option: capacity shared with another owner's portfolio
what_it_changes_in_the_model: portfolio_capacity_share below 1 with the remainder outside Telo's control; contractually a tenancy
already_implemented_by: every merchant CDMO suite
notes: shared capacity is not reserved capacity; the co-tenant's schedule is a new failure mode the engine cannot see

option: manufacture first, software later
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the frozen S5/S6 shape; capital and commissioning arrive before any revenue
already_implemented_by: Civica (after reversing from the asset-light form)
notes: commissioning costs 19.99% of the measured five-year window at the base commissioning time (pre-R004 run)

option: software first, manufacture later
what_it_changes_in_the_model: no service mechanism moves during the software phase; the model cannot show progress on any binding mode
already_implemented_by: Korber, Veeva, MasterControl, Leucine, Tulip all occupy this space
notes: the prior-art verdict is that the manufacturing OS does not survive in any of its eight sub-forms

option: virtual capacity network first, own asset only if it fails
what_it_changes_in_the_model: cdmo_reserved plans with zero commissioning; an owned site is added later only if activation fails
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: commissioning delay; capacity shortfall; contract insufficiency
already_implemented_by: Civica 2018-2023; BARDA FFMN; EU FAB
notes: the documented reversal is the warning: the asset-light form did not hold

option: laboratory or testing service first
what_it_changes_in_the_model: fixed quality cost moves off customers' ledgers; no service mechanism changes
already_implemented_by: contract labs; Creative Testing Solutions
notes: bounded by the large 503B operators already running rapid sterility on site

option: 503B responder first, durable pathway later
what_it_changes_in_the_model: pathway 503b with durable=false; eligibility is a time-varying state that the shortage listing turns off
already_implemented_by: 97 registered outsourcing facilities; QuVa, SCA, Fagron, Leiters, STAQ
notes: the only two feasible S7 cells in the run come from the forbidden permanent-listing world; never a durable core

option: product-selection and route-screening analysis first
what_it_changes_in_the_model: produces the inputs the engine most needs (route, release vector, true utilization) before any asset decision
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: capacity shortfall; sterility-related delay (by selecting the archetype)
already_implemented_by: shortage-risk scoring is implemented and patented; release-component decomposition is not
notes: an analysis method, not a company; its commercial value is as an input to route conversion

option: process-route conversion programme first
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need a route attribute per presentation, a reformulation lead time and a parametric-release scenario distinct from R3
already_implemented_by: the mechanism since 1985; Sun Pharma holds an autoclavable norepinephrine patent; nobody sells conversion as a service
notes: the only intervention in fourteen families that removes the binding release constraint; per-product work with no platform effect

option: terminal moist heat with parametric release
what_it_changes_in_the_model: release components collapse to the cycle record; no 14 d sterility hold
already_implemented_by: FDA-approved applicants since 1985 under CPG 490.200; USP <1222>
notes: portability across a second site or autoclave is unresolved (prior-art review section 7 item 1)

option: terminal moist heat with a conventional sterility test
what_it_changes_in_the_model: keeps the 14 d component but removes the aseptic-processing risk profile
already_implemented_by: the regulatory default everywhere; FDA 2004 section III; Annex 1 section 8.34
notes: terminal sterilization is preferred by regulators; the question is which products tolerate it

option: aseptic filtration with the USP <71> sterility test
what_it_changes_in_the_model: the frozen configuration: 14 d sterility as the argmax plus about 2 d serial QA
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: none; release is not binding in Phase A
already_implemented_by: most currently marketed US sterile injectables
notes: the 14 d figure is corroborated by three commercial sources and a roundtable, not by a fetched copy of USP <71>

option: aseptic filtration with a validated rapid microbiological method
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a labelled validated-rapid-micro scenario; sterility falls toward about 5 d and environmental monitoring becomes the pole
already_implemented_by: Novartis acceptances 2008-2010; ScanRDI at QuVa and SCA
notes: FDA publishes no list of products released on a rapid method; bioMerieux says approved applications exist and are confidential

option: radiation or dosimetric release
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a different route attribute entirely; not modelled
already_implemented_by: EU Annex 17 section 4.3; ISO 11137 in devices
notes: no US drug approval letter granting it was found; CPG 490.200 excludes radiation from the US parametric route

option: blow-fill-seal with terminal sterilization
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a container and process change that also changes the component set
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: sterility-related delay; component and material availability
already_implemented_by: Nephron's BFS campus
notes: Annex 1 section 8.22 requires 100% integrity testing of fusion-sealed containers

option: 503B at-risk beyond-use dating schedule
what_it_changes_in_the_model: release before a sterility result at the cost of dating: 6 d aseptic, 14 d, 28 d with a completed passing test
already_implemented_by: 503B outsourcing facilities operating under the 2018 guidance
notes: the at-risk table applies only to batches of 1,000 units or fewer; the 90-day assured BUD in the repository is a company claim, not an FDA value

option: route conversion (aseptic to terminal) as a programme
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a reformulation and container-qualification lead time before the route attribute flips
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: sterility-related delay (removed at the end of the programme)
already_implemented_by: nobody offers it as a service; the chemistry exists for one candidate
notes: falsified by any ANDA holder, CDMO or consultancy offering route conversion, or a published route mapping of the shortage list

option: owned and operating
what_it_changes_in_the_model: exists_at_t0=true, reserved=false; full capital, fixed operations and validation on the ledger
already_implemented_by: every incumbent plant
notes: fixed site operations accrue only while a site exists since R004

option: owned warm standby, exercised on a cadence
what_it_changes_in_the_model: reserved=true with reserved_site_owned=1 and exercise_batches_per_year; the line stays validated by running real batches
already_implemented_by: HHS warm-base awards to Sanofi Pasteur ($77.4M) and MedImmune ($55.1M); the CIADM warm-base line item
notes: the prior-art verdict rejects warm standby as an owned asset; keeping it requires an argument against that evidence

option: owned and idle (cold standby)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: reserved=true, exercise_batches_per_year=0; activation_failure_probability should be set high, not zero
already_implemented_by: BARDA CIADM 2012-2021; UK VMIC; DoD ammunition layaway
notes: documented to fail: no idle emergency sterile line was found that activated on schedule and met its contracted output

option: third-party reserved for a fee, not owned
what_it_changes_in_the_model: reserved_site_owned=0 since R004: only the reservation fee and the cost of batches actually run
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: insufficient surge headroom; contract insufficiency; commissioning delay
already_implemented_by: EU FAB; BARDA CIADM; DLA Warstopper; commercial CDMO clauses
notes: S3's annual cost falls about 40% under the R004 fix; every pre-2026-09-03 S3 number is superseded

option: prequalified but unreserved (technical-transfer package maintained)
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need a qualification state per partner site that the engine does not carry; today a site is either usable or not
already_implemented_by: BARDA FFMN (facilities were to become alternate locations on manufacturers' licences); CEPI VMFN
notes: whether any FFMN facility was ever added to a licence is unresolved; no GAO or HHS retrospective exists

option: campaign rotation across several prequalified sites
what_it_changes_in_the_model: would need multi-site scheduling with a validation-cadence constraint; not representable
phase_a_mechanism_addressed: insufficient surge headroom; commissioning delay; common-cause failures
already_implemented_by: only the single-site version is documented (BARDA: one annual lot per product per site)
notes: requires allocation rights over several independent owners' calendars, the same missing vehicle as multi-owner coordination

option: equipment modules held ready for install
what_it_changes_in_the_model: a capital cost with no capacity until installed; needs an install lead time the engine does not have
already_implemented_by: closest confirmed analogue is DLA prepositioning long-lead ventilator components
notes: no programme was found storing qualified aseptic filling modules ready to install

option: registered address with no qualified capacity
what_it_changes_in_the_model: not capacity at all; it is an option on future capacity
already_implemented_by: 41 of 97 registered 503B addresses never inspected, 15 of those registered over two years
notes: Leiters bought a 110,000 sq ft plant in Feb 2022 that was still not inspected 4.2 years later
